summary: Introduces a general mechanism for clients to discover optional LDAP features and extensions that cannot be discovered by existing means. This helps clients adapt to what a given server supports. It is a proposed standard that has been replaced by RFC 4512.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 3674 adds a general way for an LDAP server to advertise optional features. The server places feature identifiers in its root DSE's supportedFeatures attribute, which clients can inspect; RFC 4512 later obsoleted this memo.

questions: how do ldap clients find server capabilities
how can an ldap client discover server features
where does ldap store supported feature identifiers
subtitle: A directory attribute that lets LDAP clients discover elective server features.

tldr.problem: LDAP's existing discovery mechanisms do not provide a general way for clients to find elective server features.
tldr.mechanism: A server lists feature Object Identifiers in the supportedFeatures attribute in its root DSE, and a client can examine that list.

sections.title: Discovering Optional LDAP Features
sections.content:
LDAP already lets a client discover supported protocol versions, controls, extended operations, SASL mechanisms, and subschema information. The RFC says those mechanisms were not designed for general feature discovery.

This memo defines a general mechanism for clients to discover elective features that cannot be found through those existing mechanisms.
sections.plainLanguage: LDAP already has ways to discover some server capabilities, but not every optional feature. This memo adds a general feature list.

sections.title: The supportedFeatures Attribute
sections.content:
Each elective feature that can be discovered must have an Object Identifier (OID). A server advertises support by placing the feature's OID in the supportedFeatures attribute held in the root DSE. A client may examine the values and must ignore identifiers it does not recognize.

Servers must recognize the attribute by the name supportedFeatures and may recognize it by other names. The RFC says features associated with Standards Track protocol mechanisms must be registered; features associated with other mechanisms should be registered.
sections.plainLanguage: The server publishes identifiers for the optional features it supports. A client checks the list and ignores feature identifiers it does not understand.

sections.title: Registration and Security
sections.content: The RFC registers the supportedFeatures descriptor with OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.4203.1.3.5 and extends the LDAP Protocol Mechanism registry to support feature registrations. It says this discovery mechanism is not believed to introduce new security risk because rogue clients can discover server features by other means, such as trial and error.
sections.plainLanguage: The attribute has a registered identifier so clients and servers can refer to it consistently. The RFC says listing features does not add a new security risk.
